result.markdown: --- title: >- [summarize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute summary statistics for a sequence of numbers. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package/blob/main/tinytab/_stats.py#L47-L101){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python summarize(values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Missing values (`None` and NaN) are dropped with a warning. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[float | None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The numbers to summarize. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [SummaryResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The count, mean, standard deviation (with `n - 1` denominator), minimum and maximum. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Summarize a list of numbers: ::: {#4ae46fcc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import summarize result = summarize([3.5, 2.25, 4.0, 1.75]) result ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` SummaryResult(n=4, mean=2.875, sd=1.051, min=1.75, max=4) ``` ::: ::: Each statistic is an attribute of the result: ::: {#f77ee712 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.mean ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2.875 ``` ::: :::
